actual: Exactly that: the build succeeded and the three tests failed in 0.132s. TestResponderContract passed stages 1-2 (unknown floor and byte-identical migration served by the built-in router via the skeleton's handled=false fall-through) and failed at stage 3's corpus replay — fake.Serve errored because the permission reverse was answered -32601 by the router instead of the policy table's forwarder (expect_answer unsatisfied: 'reverse answer undecodable' — an error reply has no result payload). TestResponderDeadlineExpiry failed with handled=false (skeleton answers nothing, no expiry gate). TestResponderDedupeRace failed with 0 pending entries mid-answer (skeleton claims nothing).
semanticAssessment: Genuine RED on the planned assertion, not an incidental failure: the target executed (all three tests ran; go build and go vet passed beforehand), and every failure maps to a planned contract clause — stage 3's failure is the dedupe/first-reply-wins clause (the fake's expect_answer semantic compare rejected the router's -32601 in place of the responder's forwarder answer), the expiry failure is the deadline-gate clause (handled=false proves no policy dispatch exists), and the race failure is the delete-under-lock claim clause. Recorded nuance: stages 1-2 and the stage-8 -32601 default pass in RED because the skeleton's handled=false delegates to the conn's built-in router, whose floor and runtime-prefs answer the migration must reproduce byte-identically — that fall-through equivalence is itself contract-relevant (D-01: the responder composes with, never replaces, the router's locked posture), so those stages only become load-bearing once Serve returns handled=true. One test-harness defect was found and fixed before the RED capture: the initial pipePair gave each end both halves of one io.Pipe (crossed wiring vs the roundtrip_test pattern) and blocked the run permanently — the fix is harness-only and precedes the recorded evidence.
